algorithms.html: To perform credential-based discovery on a verifiable credential (credential) against a configured set of recognized issuers (recognizedIssuers) and an optional set of holder-provided verifiable credentials (providedDocuments), a verifier runs the following algorithm. The algorithm returns a chain, which is a list of verifiable credentials beginning with credential, followed by each recognized entity credential found by following recognizedIn references. The verifier then runs the algorithm in Section 4.3 Recognition Validation on the returned chain.

steps.html:
Let <var>current</var> be <var>credential</var> and let <var>chain</var> be a
list containing <var>credential</var>.
Let maxDepth be the maximum recognition chain depth the verifier is configured to traverse. If the length of chain exceeds maxDepth, return chain.
Let issuer be the value of the issuer property of current, and let issuerId be its identifier.

If <var>issuerId</var> is a member of <var>recognizedIssuers</var>, a candidate
anchor has been reached, so return <var>chain</var>.
If issuer does not contain a recognizedIn property, the recognition hierarchy cannot be traversed any further, so return chain.
Let listReference be the value of the recognizedIn property and let listId be its id.

Let list be the recognized entity credential identified by listId, obtained from providedDocuments if present and sufficiently fresh, or otherwise retrieved from listId. If list cannot be obtained, return chain.
Append list to chain, set current to list, and return to step 2 to evaluate the issuer of the list.

algorithms.html: To perform identifier-based discovery on a verifiable credential (credential) against a configured set of recognized issuers (recognizedIssuers), a verifier runs the following algorithm. The algorithm returns a list of candidate chains, where each chain is a list of verifiable credentials beginning with credential. The verifier then runs the algorithm in Section 4.3 Recognition Validation on the returned chains, which describes how to select among their results.

steps.html: Let <var>chains</var> be an empty list.
Let issuer be the value of the issuer property of credential, and let issuerId be its identifier.

Resolve or dereference <var>issuerId</var> to obtain a controlled identifier
document, <var>idDocument</var>. If <var>issuerId</var> cannot be resolved,
return <var>chains</var>.

Let service be a service in the service array of idDocument whose type includes both WhoisService and PathService. If no such service is present, return chains; identifier-based discovery is not supported for this issuer.
Let endpoint be the serviceEndpoint of service and retrieve the verifiable presentation, presentation, published at endpoint. If retrieval fails, return chains.

Verify the proof on <var>presentation</var> and confirm that it is bound to
<var>issuerId</var>. If verification fails, return <var>chains</var>.

Let candidates be the recognized entity credentials contained in presentation in which issuerId appears as the id of a recognized entity in the credentialSubject. If candidates is empty, return chains.

For each list in candidates, do the following. If the issuer of list is a member of recognizedIssuers, append the chain consisting of credential followed by list to chains. Otherwise, if the issuer object of list contains a recognizedIn property, perform credential-based discovery on list against recognizedIssuers and append the chain consisting of credential followed by the elements of the returned chain to chains.
Return <var>chains</var>.

algorithms.html: To perform recognition validation on a chain (chain) produced by any discovery mechanism, for a specific action (action, for example issue), against a configured set of recognized issuers (recognizedIssuers), a verifier runs the following algorithm. The algorithm returns a result with two boolean outcomes: entityRecognized, indicating whether the issuer of the first verifiable credential in chain is ultimately recognized by a member of recognizedIssuers, and actionRecognized, indicating whether that issuer is recognized to perform action and, where a recognized action declares an outputValidation, whether the verifiable credential conforms to it.

steps.html: Let result be a structure with recognized set to false and actionRecognized set to false.
If chain contains fewer than two verifiable credentials, return result. A recognition chain consists of at least a verifiable credential and a recognized entity credential that recognizes its issuer.
Let maxDepth be the maximum recognition chain depth the verifier is configured to accept. If the length of chain exceeds maxDepth, return result.

Let seen be an empty set. For each verifiable credential in chain, let id be the identifier of its issuer. If id is already a member of seen, the chain contains a cycle, so return result. Otherwise, add id to seen.

Let window be the period during which every verifiable credential in chain was valid at the same time. To determine it, let window start at the latest validFrom property in chain and end at the earliest validUntil property in chain. A verifiable credential that expresses no validFrom property does not constrain the start, and one that expresses no validUntil property does not constrain the end. If window ends before it starts, no such period exists, so return result.

For each adjacent pair of verifiable credentials in chain, where subject is the earlier verifiable credential and list is the later one, confirm that list is a recognized entity credential and that the credentialSubject of list contains a recognized entity whose id is equal, using simple string comparison, to the identifier of the issuer of subject. If it does not, the two verifiable credentials are unrelated, so return result.

Confirm that the issuer of the final verifiable credential in chain is a member of recognizedIssuers. If it is not, the chain does not terminate at an anchor that the verifier recognizes, so return result. Otherwise, set result.recognized to true.

Let credential be the first verifiable credential in chain, let list be the second, and let entity be the recognized entity in the credentialSubject of list whose id is the identifier of the issuer of credential. Set result.actionRecognized to true if any recognized action declared by the recognizedTo property of entity meets all of the following conditions.
Its action value is equal to action.
Its validity period, if it expresses a validFrom or validUntil property, includes at least part of window.
It declares no outputValidation, or credential conforms to every schema referenced by its outputValidation.
Return <var>result</var>.
